steps.say: EGPA classically is asthma with eosinophils and vasculitis in three acts. Adult-onset asthma opens, tissue eosinophilia follows, and nerve and kidney vasculitis closes. ANCA is the divider of the two faces. This figure shows the nasal polyps of the opening act.
steps.tx: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (**EGPA**, Churg-Strauss syndrome, eosinophilic small vessel vasculitis) blends severe adult-onset **asthma** (reversible airway narrowing), blood and tissue **eosinophilia** (eosinophil excess), and necrotizing granulomatous small-to-medium vessel inflammation. Adult asthma with rising eosinophils indicates EGPA surveillance long before vasculitis declares itself.

vis.alt: Sagittal nasal cavity with oedematous polyps arising from middle meatus and ethmoid sinus.
vis.caption: Nasal polyps with adult-onset asthma open the prodromal phase. Eosinophil counts are tracked from this stage. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Three phases are the march from allergy through eosinophils to vasculitis. Eosinophils above 1500 or above 10 percent are the definition of the middle act. Nerves, purpura, and kidneys are the markers of the final act. Phase is the decider of therapy, not just diagnosis.
steps.tx: The march opens with allergy (adult asthma, runny nose, nasal **polyps**), escalates to eosinophil excess in blood above **1,500** per microliter or **10 percent** with lung and gut infiltration, and closes with systemic vessel inflammation (**mononeuritis multiplex**, nerve infarcts; purpura; glomerulonephritis). Eosinophils above 1,500 with new neuropathy indicate the vasculitic phase at once.

steps.say: ANCA is positive in 30 to 50 percent, always of MPO type. Positive disease is the attacker of nerves, kidneys, and skin vessels together. Negative disease infiltrates the heart with eosinophils instead. The antibody result splits management.
steps.tx: **ANCA** positivity hits **30 to 50 percent** of EGPA, almost always p-ANCA against **MPO** (myeloperoxidase). ANCA-positive disease brings vasculitic glomerulonephritis, mononeuritis multiplex, and purpura, while ANCA-negative disease brings eosinophilic tissue infiltration with severe cardiac disease. The ANCA result splits surveillance between kidneys with nerves and the heart.

steps.say: The heart leads mortality through eosinophilic myocarditis with fibrosis and clots. Late gadolinium enhancement on MRI is the marker of it. Heart failure with eosinophilia is EGPA until proven otherwise. Cardiac imaging is never skipped.
steps.tx: Cardiac disease leads EGPA mortality: eosinophilic **endomyocarditis** (eosinophil heart muscle inflammation) with myocardial **fibrosis** (scar), restrictive **cardiomyopathy** (stiff heart), intracardiac thrombi, and failure, seen as late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac **MRI** (magnetic resonance). Heart failure with eosinophilia indicates cardiac MRI at once, because echo misses early infiltration.

steps.say: Nerve ischaemia is seen in 70 to 80 percent as mononeuritis multiplex or asymmetric polyneuropathy. Wrist and foot drop are the signatures. Epineurial vessels are the target. New foot drop with asthma and eosinophils is EGPA.
steps.tx: Peripheral neuropathy strikes up to **70 to 80 percent**, the commonest vasculitic feature, as **mononeuritis multiplex** (sequential single nerve infarcts) or asymmetric polyneuropathy from ischemic **epineurial** arteritis (inflamed nerve sheath vessels). Wrist drop with foot drop in sequence indicates vasculitic neuropathy. New drop with asthma and eosinophilia is EGPA until proven otherwise.

vis.alt: Nerve section with vasa nervorum vasculitis causing wrist drop and foot drop.
vis.caption: Vasa nervorum vasculitis starves nerves into wrist and foot drop. Sequential drops mark the vasculitic phase. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The Five-Factor Score for risk stratification is the decider of induction intensity. A score of 1 or higher with heart, gut, or kidney disease requires cyclophosphamide with steroids. Milder disease takes steroids alone. Scoring precedes every induction.
steps.tx: The **Five-Factor Score** (FFS, prognosis scale) guides induction: severe organ or life-threatening disease at **FFS 1 or higher**, with cardiomyopathy, gastrointestinal involvement, or renal insufficiency, requires systemic glucocorticoids plus IV **cyclophosphamide**. Milder disease takes glucocorticoids alone. Every new EGPA case is scored before induction, because the score picks the regimen.

steps.say: Fully human mepolizumab 300 mg every 4 weeks earned its place in MIRRA for relapsing disease with steroid tapering. Anti-IL-5 benralizumab matched it in MANDARA. Both target the IL-5 axis. Steroid dependence is the trigger for either.
steps.tx: **Mepolizumab** (IL-5 blockade) dosed at **300 mg** under the skin each **4 weeks** lengthened remission with steroid tapering in **MIRRA** for relapsing or refractory non-organ-threatening EGPA. **Benralizumab** (IL-5 receptor alpha blockade, eosinophil killer by cellular cytotoxicity) matched mepolizumab in **MANDARA**. Steroid-dependent relapsing disease indicates either IL-5 agent.

steps.say: Asthma with eosinophils above 1500 is watched for nerves, kidneys, and heart together. ANCA status is the splitter of the watch between vasculitic and eosinophilic organs. Steroids are the openers of therapy while scores are the pickers of cyclophosphamide. IL-5 agents are the holders of relapsing disease.
steps.tx: Adult asthma with eosinophils above **1,500** is watched across nerves (**70 to 80 percent** hit), kidneys, and heart together. **ANCA** in **30 to 50 percent** splits the watch: positive toward glomerulonephritis with neuropathy, negative toward cardiac infiltration. Glucocorticoids open all therapy, **FFS 1 or higher** adds **cyclophosphamide**, and IL-5 blockade (**300 mg** monthly mepolizumab or benralizumab) holds relapsing cases.
